summary: The screening prompt, data-block escaping, transient-failure handling, cap ordering (no extra LLM call for capped or skipped listings), status() before the first tick and the public wording (no forbidden ADR-32 vocabulary) all hold up; the two real defects are that the clone check counts purchases that ended unpaid as "already bought" (contradicting the published "a function is bought once" and blocking later sellers after one failing seller), and that titled index entries shrink the compacted index to ~100 entries so listings inside the 30-day lookback can be re-bought and per-seller limits reset. Two low findings: the eligible early-return bypasses the clone check after a transient create failure, and the order-blind Jaccard refuses direction-reversed titles without the judge.

title: Clone check and already_bought treat purchases that ended unpaid as "bought"
problem: `bought` is every index entry with a title, regardless of outcome. Index entries are written at hire time (line 471) and keep their title when the purchase ends as `expired`, `declined`, `no_delivery`, `vanished`, `quote_above_cap`, `upfront_refused` or `unpaid_caps`. Concrete: seller A lists "Probe an x402 endpoint (Base)", the desk hires, A never accepts, `end(..., 'expired')`. Seller B then lists "Probe x402 endpoints on Base" (tokens identical after plural strip, Jaccard 1.0): line 423 skips it permanently with "duplicate: the desk already bought this function", and line 427 also lists A's title in `already_bought` for the judge. The desk never received the function, so the public texts (SKILL.md "clones of a function it already bought", commitments "a function is bought once, not each copy") do not match the code, and one failing seller blocks every later seller of that function for the 60-day index horizon.
fix: Filter to purchases the desk actually paid or still has open: `Object.values(st.index).filter((e): e is IndexEntry & { title: string } => !!e.title && (!e.outcome || e.outcome.startsWith('paid')))`, and use the same list for `already_bought`.

title: Titled index entries make compaction halve the index to 100 entries, dropping purchases still inside the 30-day lookback
problem: Each index entry now carries `title` (80 chars) and `category`, about 285 bytes each; 400 entries are ~114 KB, so the loop at lines 178-192 always halves `indexKept` until the state fits. Measured with compactState on an otherwise empty state: 400 titled entries keep 100 (28.5 KB), 200 keep 100, 150 keep 150; before this change 400 untitled entries kept 200. The IndexEntry doc (line 84) calls it a "never-trimmed-by-count record" and it is the only source for `already bought` (line 352), the per-seller limit (line 361), the wallet limit (line 467) and the clone check. At live defaults (5 new sellers/day x 2) 100 entries cover ~10 days against a 30-day listing lookback and a 60-day horizon: once the entry for a listing younger than 30 days is trimmed, `ineligible` no longer sees it, the desk hires it a second time (the idempotency key only replays inside the API's idempotency window) and the seller's per-seller count restarts. The compaction test (firstbuy.test.ts line 482) builds index entries without titles and asserts < 64 KB instead of MAX_BYTES, so it does not show this.
fix: Never count-trim index entries younger than `lookbackDays` (only entries between lookbackDays and 2*lookbackDays are candidates for `indexKept`), and shrink `skipped`/`eligible`/done first. Add titled entries (and `eligible`) to the compaction test and assert `<= MAX_BYTES` plus that every entry younger than lookbackDays survives.

title: eligible early-return skips the clone check, so two copies of one function can both be bought
problem: `screen()` returns null on `st.eligible[l.id]` before the mechanical clone check at lines 422-424. Sequence: listing L is screened eligible, `jobs.create` throws transiently (503, network), discovery aborts and `eligible[L]` is persisted at the end of the tick. Next tick a newer listing M of the same function (listed after L, sorted first by `sort: 'newest'`) passes the clone check (L is not in the index), is judged eligible and bought; then L hits the eligible early-return, bypasses the clone check against M's index title, and is bought too.
fix: Run the free clone check first and only then consult `st.eligible`: move line 421 below line 424.

title: Title Jaccard is order-blind: directional services from different sellers are refused as clones without the judge
problem: `titleTokens` drops `to` and symbols, so "English → German translation (glossary)" and "German → English translation (glossary)" have identical token sets, overlap 1.0 >= CLONE_JACCARD, and the second is skipped permanently at line 423 with "the desk already bought this function" and the judge is never asked. Same for any pair that differs only in direction or order ("Translate DE to EN" / "Translate EN to DE", "USDC to EUR rate" / "EUR to USDC rate"). Ordinary distinct titles ("German translation" vs "German to English translation with glossary" = 0.5) are not affected; the failure is confined to word-order pairs. The test at line 441-442 only checks a plural variant and an unrelated pair.
fix: Make the mechanical skip need order too, e.g. also require token-bigram Jaccard >= 0.6 (or exact equality of the token sequence), and otherwise let the judge decide with the candidate flagged in `already_bought`; add a test that a direction-reversed title is not a mechanical clone.

summary: The ADR-35 listing cap does not hold: concurrent creates bypass it (14 parallel POSTs from one unproven seller all succeeded) and a single completed free job from any second keypair lifts it to 50, while every public text says a third party must have paid. The demand signal and screening are mostly sound, but the ready-made bounty body can be rejected on a one-character category, the first-buy clone check ignores everything bought before this deploy, search terms are published verbatim and instantly with no redaction, and the empty-search hint misstates when upfront proposals are paid.

title: Listing cap is not enforced under concurrent creates (count-then-insert without a lock)
problem: assertListingCap reads count(*) and createListing inserts later with several awaits in between and no per-seller lock (lib/mutex.ts withLock exists but is not used here). Two or more concurrent POST /v1/listings at 9 active both see n=9 < 10 and both insert. Reproduced: 14 parallel POST /v1/listings from a fresh unproven seller returned 14 x 201 (cap 10). The same applies to the reactivation path in updateListing (line 205). The rewritten P7 test in review-regressions.test.ts avoids the cap (9 parallel, then a same-key burst) instead of testing it, so nothing catches this.
fix: Wrap createListing and the status->active branch of updateListing in withLock(`listings:${env}:${seller.id}`, ...) so the count and the insert/update are serialised per seller; add a test that fires 14 parallel creates and expects at most 10 x 201.

title: Cap rises on a free job, not on a payment; every public text says 'until another agent has paid you'
problem: activeListingCap raises the cap when asSeller.third_party_counterparties >= 1. That counter (reviews/service.ts:171,193) also counts agents met only through completed free jobs (paidValue(j) === 0 -> freeIds -> thirdPartyIds). So a seller with one price-0 listing completed by any second keypair (its own sandbox alt, no wallet, no USDC) gets 50 slots. The create route description, MCP create_listing, llms.txt, skill.md, commitments listing_caps_and_ranking, the 409 hint ('rises to 50 once another agent pays you') and changelog 0.4.2 all say a third party must have PAID; the code does not require it.
fix: Gate on paid third-party demand: e.g. (rep?.asSeller.third_party_volume_usdc ?? 0) > 0 (or add a paid-third-party counter), or change every text to 'has completed a job with you'. Add a test: a completed free job from another agent must not lift the cap.

title: post_a_bounty body_example fails CreateBountyBody when the search carried a one-character category
problem: body_example.category is (category ?? 'other').toLowerCase().slice(0, 48). The search query schema allows category up to 48 chars with no minimum, so GET /v1/listings?q=quantum%20forecast&category=x (or category=%20) returns an empty page with category 'x', and POST /v1/bounties rejects it with 400 (CreateBountyBody category min(2)). The hint says the body can be sent as is.
fix: const cat = (category ?? '').trim().toLowerCase().slice(0, 48); category: cat.length >= 2 ? cat : 'other'. Cover it in demand/routes.test.ts.

title: Clone check and judge already_bought are blind to everything bought before this deploy
problem: screen() builds `bought` from index entries that carry a title. fetchState only creates an index entry (with title) when st.index[p.listing_id] is missing; every existing purchase already has an index entry without title, and it is never backfilled. On the first ticks after deploy the mechanical Jaccard check compares against nothing and the judge receives an empty already_bought, so the exact day-four case (a clone of 'JSON record change report by unique key', bought before ADR-35) is bought again.
fix: Backfill the title: for (const p of st.purchases) { const e = st.index[p.listing_id]; if (!e) st.index[p.listing_id] = {...}; else if (!e.title) e.title = p.title } (category stays unknown for old entries; the judge input tolerates ''). Add a fetchState test with a pre-ADR-35 index entry.

title: Search terms are published verbatim after a single search, within seconds, with no redaction of identifying tokens
problem: normaliseTerm only lowercases and collapses whitespace; a query such as 'jobs by @alice', '0x9f3c...' (a wallet), an e-mail, or a pasted as_live_ key is stored and shown on public GET /v1/demand with searches=1 for up to 30 days (rows are never pruned, days<=30). searchedTerms flushes on every read, so a term appears the moment anyone polls /v1/demand, which lets an observer correlate a term with the registration, bounty or job that follows it. The page and llms.txt state 'Nothing here identifies a searcher' and 'never who searched', which holds only while the term text itself is not identifying.
fix: In normaliseTerm drop or replace tokens matching handles (@\w+), EVM addresses (0x[0-9a-f]{40}), e-mails, and key prefixes (as_(live|test)_\w+), and flush only from the scheduler (remove the flushSearches call in searchedTerms) so a term cannot be timed to the second; optionally hide terms with searches < 2 from the public list.

title: Hint promises payment only 'when you award a proposal and the delivery is sealed'; upfront proposals are payable right after award
problem: createJobFromBountyAward (jobs/service.ts:536-557) puts an awarded upfront proposal into status awaiting_payment with a payment deadline before any delivery exists. The empty-search hint and the llms.txt bounties line (discovery/text.ts:168, 'you pay only when you award and the delivery is sealed') therefore promise a timing the code does not keep for upfront proposals.
fix: Reword both: 'you pay when the job asks for it: against the sealed delivery for on_delivery proposals, right after award for an upfront proposal (the proposal shows which)'.

title: zero_results counts filtered empty pages as 'returned no listing at all'
problem: recordSearch(env, q.q, page.length === 0) runs for any first page with q, including ones narrowed by category, tag, max_price, pricing_model, payment or graduated. GET /v1/listings?q=german%20translation&max_price=1 returns nothing while a German translation listing exists, and 'german translation' then appears in unmet_searches (DemandTermView says 'returned no listing at all'; the demand page calls it 'the gap you could fill'). Sellers are pointed at a gap that is not there.
fix: Only flag zeroResults when no filter other than q (and env) is set, or run the filter-free count for the term; state the rule in how_this_is_made.

title: Cached 'eligible' verdict skips the clone check, so a function can be bought twice
problem: screen() returns null as soon as st.eligible[l.id] is set, before the Jaccard clone check. A listing screened eligible but held back by a cap (per-seller, daily, open purchases) is bought on a later tick even if the desk bought the same function from another seller in between; the commitments text says 'a function is bought once, not each copy'.
fix: Run the clone check against st.index before the eligible short-circuit (it is cheap and needs no model); only the judge call should be skipped for cached-eligible listings.

title: Cache-Control: public on a response whose env depends on the Authorization header
problem: GET /v1/demand picks env from the API key (optionalAuth) unless ?env= is given, then sends 'public, max-age=60' without Vary: Authorization. A shared HTTP cache between agents (proxy) may serve the sandbox body to a live request or vice versa for the same URL. Same pattern as /v1/commitments, but this page is the one sellers are told to read before listing.
fix: Add c.header('Vary', 'Authorization'), or use 'private, max-age=60' when a key was presented.
